name: Travel basics
description: UK rail questions from the earlier evaluation (test_data_v2, with its gold answers), a live weather question, and three questions the input guardrail should block (a visa question and a Swiss timetable are outside the UK rail and weather scope).

questions.question: Which train companies operate in South Yorkshire?
questions.expected: Five main national train companies operate in South Yorkshire: Northern, CrossCountry, LNER, East Midlands Railway, and TransPennine Express [Source 1].

questions.question: Can I use a Railcard to save money on my train tickets?
questions.expected: Yes! Railcards cost £35 for one year (or £80 for three years) and give you 1/3 off eligible train tickets across Great Britain [Source 1]. There are various types depending on your age or circumstances, like 16-25, 60+, family, or disabled Railcards [Source 1][Source 3].

questions.question: How can I save money when booking a train ticket?
questions.expected: You can save by booking Advance tickets up to 12 weeks ahead, travelling Off-Peak, getting a Railcard (up to 1/3 off), using split-ticketing, or GroupSave if travelling with 3-9 people [Source 1, Source 3, Source 4].

questions.question: How far in advance should I book my train ticket to get a cheaper fare?
questions.expected: Book about 12 weeks ahead of your travel date—Advance tickets are usually cheapest when first released [Source 1][Source 2][Source 4][Source 5].

questions.question: I'm travelling with children. Are there any discounts available?
questions.expected: Yes! The Family & Friends Railcard costs £35/year and gives 1/3 off adult fares plus 60% off child fares for up to 4 adults and 4 children (ages 5-15) [Source 2]. There's also an Off-Peak Family Travelcard for certain UK train companies [Source 5].

questions.question: What is the Kids for a Quid offer?
questions.expected: It lets up to 4 children aged 5-15 travel for just £1 on a single or return journey in Standard Class during Off-Peak times, as long as they're with an adult [Source 1]. It's offered on select Southeastern, West Midlands Railway, London Northwestern, Chiltern, and ScotRail routes [Source 1].

questions.question: What age do children need to be for Kids for a Quid?
questions.expected: Children need to be aged 5-15 to qualify for Kids for a Quid tickets [Source 1].

questions.question: Can I use Kids for a Quid on every train company?
questions.expected: No, only select companies offer it—Southeastern, West Midlands Railway, London Northwestern Railway, and Chiltern Railway routes are bookable via Trainline, and ScotRail also offers it but not online [Source 1].

questions.question: What is a Family Travelcard and who can use it?
questions.expected: A Family Travelcard is a group Off-Peak Return ticket that includes unlimited travel across London's National Rail, Underground, DLR, Tramlink and buses (Zones 1-6) for the day. It's for 1-2 adults with up to 4 children aged 5-15 travelling together [Source 2][Source 1].

questions.question: Can I use a Family Travelcard on the London Underground?
questions.expected: Yes! An Off-Peak Family Travelcard includes unlimited travel on National Rail, London Underground, DLR, Tramlink, and London Buses within Fare Zones 1-6 for the day [Source 1].

questions.question: Is there a pantry car on trains?
questions.expected: Answers for UK trains only (on-board catering such as a buffet, café bar or at-seat trolley, which depends on the operator), citing UK sources; nothing about Indian Railways pantry cars.

questions.question: What will the weather be like in Zurich tomorrow?
questions.expected: Live forecast from Open-Meteo (temperature range and rain).
